faq.a: Abdel is associated with the Arabic form عَبْدُ, whose core sense is abdel; servant (of god).

faq.q: What is the origin of Abdel?
faq.a: Abdel is associated with Arabic. Abdel is Arabic عَبْد (ʿAbd), meaning 'servant', used as the first element of compound male names such as Abdelrahman.
Yes — the underlying form عَبْدُ is Arabic.
Abdel can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Abdel should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root ع ب د is Quranic, but ʿAbd is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Abdel mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Abdel is rendered عبد and carries the sense عبد، بندہ.

faq.q: What does Abdel mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Abdel is rendered عبد and carries the sense عبد، بنده.

faq.q: What are the variants of Abdel?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Abdel, abdel. Script forms are عبد, عَبْدُ, अब्देल.

faq.q: Is Abdel a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
